slides.title: Publications tracker (90-161.Z): pilot decision
slides.subtitle:
For the commander and group commanders
Draft r3 (palette preview) · 12 November 2026 · about 10 minutes
slides.notes: Purpose: decide whether to pilot the tracker at this wing and start the approval reviews. No government data is in this brief.

list: Approve a pilot at this wing once the reviews below are under way.

slides.notes: Three asks: pilot, reviews, backup person.

slides.title: Why use it: one place for every publication action
slides.lead: It runs the steps of DAFMAN 90-161 (the Air Force publishing manual) for the wing and keeps every step on record.
head: Today
With 90-161.Z
Rule it follows
rows: Status lives in e-mail and in people's heads
Anyone can see where each publication stands, at any time
Automatic requests and weekday reminders; overdue items go to the right person
Formatting is fixed by hand, page by page
Software applies the official format and checks every rule
Review dates are tracked; the review opens 6 months early
Wing checklist, action officer guide, template and workbook
Replaced by one app with step-by-step screens
slides.notes: The rules come from DAFMAN 90-161, not from the tool.

slides.title: Does it work? Built in parts; each part is tested before the next
slides.lead: Tested on fake data only. Real publications wait for the approvals.
head: Part
Status
What the test showed
rows: Built on a wing site by the setup flow on 11 Nov; all counts matched
6 of 6 test documents produced; 2 small layout defects being fixed
Passed 12 of 12 checks on fake drafts
Designed; built after the access tests
Test kit ready; the PFM runs it next
slides.notes: Honest status: the foundation works; the parts people touch are not built yet.

slides.title: If it breaks, work continues by hand and no data is lost
head: What breaks
What people notice
What happens
rows: The app or the reminders stop
The PFM works from the SharePoint lists and e-mails by hand, as today
The PFM leaves or their account closes
The backup person takes over with a written handover; a daily check flags it
Someone deletes or changes data by mistake
Every change is kept; deleted items can be restored for 93 days; a regular export is planned
A Microsoft or DoD365 policy change
Each feature has a fallback; the tool shows what to do
Publications stay on the wing site as normal files; lists can be exported
slides.notes: The tool adds automation on top of normal SharePoint. Removing it leaves the data in place.

slides.title: What it costs
head: Cost
Amount
Note
rows: Uses only the standard DoD365 tools; the design forbids paid add-ons. The license manager confirms
PFM time to build and pilot
Measured during the pilot and reported back
A few hours to learn it
Needed so the tool survives a move or a leave period
Replaces manual tracking; measured in the pilot
One set of reviews can serve every wing if NGB sponsors it
slides.notes: No new money expected. The main cost is people's time, which the pilot measures.

slides.title: Is it approved for use? Not yet
slides.lead: It runs only on tools the wing already uses (DoD365 and GenAI.mil). These reviews are still needed:
head: Review
Status
The question for that office
rows: May the tool and its setup scripts be used on the network, and how should scripts be delivered?
The design files are public: do they need a security and policy review?
Is the work official duty, and under what license may other wings use it?
The lists hold names and work e-mails: is a privacy assessment needed?
Which records rules apply to the lists, and where must project records be kept?
slides.notes: Nothing real goes into the tool before these answers.

slides.title: Top risks and what we do about them
slides.notes: Full risk list is in the installer brief and the project records.

slides.title: Who keeps it running

options.name: A. The PFM alone
options.what: One person builds, fixes and supports it in addition to their duties.
options.con: Stops when that person moves; does not scale to other wings.

options.name: B. Named owner and backup, NGB sponsor
options.what: A named owner and a backup person; NGB sponsors it for other wings.
options.pro: Survives moves; one set of approvals for all wings.
options.con: Needs a sponsor and a little time from two people.

options.name: C. Each wing copies it
options.what: Wings copy it once and maintain their own.
options.con: Copies drift apart; the same approvals repeat at every wing.

slides.note: Recommendation by the project; it is not a decision until you approve it.
